posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
You've got two slow-build heroes (Tachyon, Unity), a support hero (Scholar), and one damage dealer (Haka). Since you're playing Baron Blade on advanced, you are in a race.

So, I recommend Haka focuses on doing as much damage as possible, even if that limits his longer-term capabilities because of missed opportunities for extra card draws. If you can get to BB's flip, this game will become relatively easy, but you've got to get there.

The Scholar may need to prepare for tanking lots of damage. Your only way to win may be to leave BB's targets on the field so that the trash doesn't fill, in which case Scholar's ability to direct damage to himself and negate it will become essential.

Tachyon may need to resort to relatively early uses of the Lightspeed Barage. It's likely to be more important to do a couple of 5-point shots and push BB to his other side than to save them for the massive later shots.

Unity has a fantastic start. I don't remember how much BB or the Tomb have in terms of hitting the lowest, but getting Platform and Raptor out early to start doing damage to Blade is fantastic.

posts.name: Mezike
posts.cooked:
Well, Unity is doing 6 damage per turn off the bat (if she can keep her bots alive), and with the HoB I can wind it up to do at least 18 damage with Mere over the next four turns, getting us 42 damage from just two heroes and even more with extra card draws provided by the rest of the team. I'm pretty sure the other heroes will have some options so this is totally do-able.

Tachyon is a no-brainer with fleet of foot and ptl out first to get some more options into our hands and to get her card burn on. I would also advise the Scholar to concentrate on drawing as many cards as possible - cards like Grace Under Fire, Turn Loose, Proverbs, Don't Dismiss Anything could be game winners here but it won't help if they are still in his deck. Dig for victory - dig for cards! Worst case he will take a few hits then lay down some healing combos that will properly charge his elemental form to do a bigger hit of damage, which may be all we need to get the flip.

Overall I recommend we take a totally cavalier attitude to our HP and think about healing options after the flip. If that means F6 Unity indulging in a bit of self harm to get a bot out then go for it. Our biggest risk is a lack of deck control, we just have to roll with whatever BB throws at us and hope we don't get stomped by the card draw.
